live_divergence_note.universe: Live scans the dynamic RS-ranked universe (universe.py, top_n=8, weekly rebalance), NOT the 12 tickers in frozen.tickers. Those 12 are the OOS validation universe only. Chosen deliberately; universe_backtest.py measures the rule point-in-time.
live_divergence_note.atr_stop: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-02. The 2026-08-28 entry said 'Live now matches frozen.atr_stop=1.25' — that was true of scanner.py (which reads signal_core.DEFAULTS) but NOT of app.py, whose sidebar default was still a hardcoded 1.0. So the app showed stops, R:R and pass/fail on a value the harness never tested, while the scanner used 1.25. Two other sidebar literals had drifted the same way: hq_min_rr app 1.5 vs core 1.0 (the scanner Telegrams high-quality at 1.0) and volume_mult app 1.0 vs core 1.2 (different 'Strong' tag, which feeds high_quality). All three are now sourced from signal_core.DEFAULTS in app.py rather than written as literals, and consistency_check.py fails CI if any of them becomes a literal again. Verified: app._signal_params() == signal_core.DEFAULTS.
live_divergence_note.why_this_note: The atr_stop discrepancy went unnoticed because nothing recorded which value was chosen or why. Anything that diverges from frozen{} belongs here, dated. NOTE the 2026-08-28 entry was itself incomplete — it checked one of the two live surfaces and declared the drift closed. A note is only as good as the surfaces it actually checked; say which ones.
live_divergence_note.open_divergences_2026_09_02: STILL OPEN: backtest.py fetches with auto_adjust=True (dividend-adjusted) while every live path uses auto_adjust=False, so the OOS result was measured on a differently-adjusted price series than the one live signals fire on. Also app.py and scanner.py still compute the weekly trend and the SPY regime with DIFFERENT rules (EMA10w/EMA20w cross vs price/EMA20w; 3-state ADX-gated regime vs 2-state), so the values injected into signal_core.evaluate() can differ between the two. Tracked, not yet fixed.
